title: Product PRD: Runtime Cost Controls and Packaging (Q2 2026)
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview
========
This document defines the product requirements, high-level design, roadmap, packaging and pricing guidance, and release notes for Redwood Inference's Runtime Cost Controls and Packaging initiative (targeting GA in Q2/Q3 2026). The initiative delivers a coherent set of controls and presets that let engineering and platform teams reduce per-token costs while meeting latency and reliability SLOs. It combines UI/Console features, API flags, autoscaling policies, and packaging changes for Dedicated and Private offerings.

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
Goals:
- Provide first-class runtime controls that let customers trade cost vs latency with predictable economic outcomes.
- Ship console UX for cost profiles and a public API that can be applied per-route or per-model.
- Introduce packaged pricing tiers and add-on options that reflect the new controls for Dedicated and Private customers.
- Validate on three pilot customers (media startup, enterprise search, and chat assistant platform) before GA.

Non-goals:
- This phase does not change core model pricing per token. It exposes controls and inference configurations, not model-level price changes.
- Not implementing custom kernel-level quantization tooling in this release — that remains in the Quantization Profiles epic.

Success metrics
---------------
- 20% average per-token cost reduction for pilot customers without exceeding latency SLO by more than 10% (measured over 30-day windows).
- Adoption: 25% of Dedicated customers opt into a cost-profile within 90 days of release.
- Revenue: Packaging changes enable a new add-on representing >=5% of Dedicated bookings in first 6 months.
- Quality/regressions: <1% of requests experience quality regression (as defined by evaluation harness prompts flagged for quality alerts).

User personas and primary use cases
----------------------------------
- ML/Platform Engineers: configure cost/latency profiles per service route and monitor effects.
- Product Engineers: choose presets to meet budget targets for specific features (e.g., chat, summarization).
- SRE/Platform Teams: apply org-level policies and guardrails across projects.

Functional requirements (high level)
-----------------------------------
1. Cost Profiles API and Console
   - Create, read, update, delete (CRUD) cost profiles.
   - Profiles contain: batching target (tokens/request and batch size), KV cache TTLs, quantization preference (e.g., float16/int8), fallback model mapping, and target p50/p95 latency budgets.
   - Profiles may be scoped at: global account, project, model route.

2. Per-route Application
   - Routes must accept a profile_id header or reference in route config.
   - API supports preview mode that simulates estimated cost and latency before applying.

3. Autoscaler and Runtime Integration
   - Autoscaler must accept profile signals: preferred batch window and concurrency target.
   - Runtime should expose metrics for observed batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, and quantization fallbacks.

4. Analytics and Alerts
   - Per-profile dashboards with cost-per-1k-token, latency percentile breakdowns, and request quality regressions linked to eval prompt sets.
   - Alerts for cost overrun (e.g., actual cost > 120% of projected for rolling 24h) and latency SLO breaches.

5. Packaging and Billing
   - New pricing SKU: "Optimize Add-on" for Dedicated/Private customers that includes advanced profiles, extended console retention, and SRE deployment assistance.
   - Billing events: enabling SKU should be billable monthly with clear consumption metrics reported to billing pipeline.

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- Latency overhead: profile evaluation and routing must add <2ms P50 request overhead.
- Security: profiles are part of account config and subject to RBAC. Changes must be auditable via audit log events.
- Backwards compatibility: routes without profile references use existing default runtime behavior.

Design spec (high level)
------------------------
Architecture components:
- Cost Profile Service (CPS): lightweight service storing profiles and evaluating preview estimates. Exposes REST API and events for config changes.
- Runtime adapters: small hooks in serving runtime to ingest profile signals (batch window, quantization preference, cache TTL) at request admission.
- Autoscaler extension: a component in eng-sre autoscaler to translate profile signals into target concurrency and scaling thresholds.
- Console UI: profile editor, per-route assignment, preview modal, and profile analytics dashboard.
- Billing integration: event pipeline that emits SKU enablement and monthly usage summaries to finance.

Configuration schema (example YAML shown as text snippet):

# cost-profile.yaml (example)
name: "low-latency"
batching: { target_tokens_per_batch: 1024, max_batch_size: 8, batch_window_ms: 15 }
kv_cache: { ttl_seconds: 300, enabled: true }
quantization: "float16"
fallback_models: ["redwood-std-1.3", "redwood-eco-1.0"]
latency_budget_ms: { p50: 40, p95: 120 }

Note: stored as JSON in CPS; console shows YAML for readability.

API surface (examples)
- GET /v1/cost_profiles
- POST /v1/cost_profiles {name, settings...}
- POST /v1/cost_profiles/preview {route_config, sample_traffic_profile}
- PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id} {profile_id}
- Events: cost_profile.updated (published to internal event bus)

Runtime integration details
- At request admission, runtime calls CPS cache for profile_id. If missing, uses default configuration.
- Runtime will apply batching target by adjusting request queuing policy; KV cache TTLs are advisory to cache layer.
- Quantization preference is a hint: runtime may select appropriate model binary (e.g., int8 quantized image) if available.

Rollout plan and ownership
--------------------------
Owners:
- Product: Avery Chen (product lead)
- Eng - Serving Runtime: Priya Nair (tech lead)
- Eng - SRE/Autoscaler: Jamal Rivers
- Eng - Console/UX: Diego Martinez
- Finance/Billing: Lina Park
- Customer Success (pilots): Sana Kapoor

Rollout stages:
1. Internal dogfood (4 weeks) — apply to internal staging routes and monitoring dashboards.
2. Pilot customers (8–12 weeks) — 3 customers; enable preview and co-deploy with SREs.
3. Beta (6 weeks) — open to all Dedicated customers with opt-in.
4. GA — public docs, billing SKU enabled, migration guides published.

Migration and compatibility steps for customers:
1. Identify critical routes and create corresponding cost profiles in preview mode.
2. Run simulation with sample-traffic (provided CLI helper: rwi cost-profile simulate --profile profile.json --traffic sample.json).
3. Apply profile to non-production route and monitor for two weeks.
4. Ramp to production using canary and A/B rollout.

Monitoring and SLOs
------------------
- Observability: dashboards per profile and aggregated account-level views.
- SLOs: less than 1% of requests exceeding p95 latency of the profile by 2x due to profile changes during normal operation.
- Error budgets: profile changes count as a deploy and are included in error budget calculations for affected services.

Security and compliance
-----------------------
- RBAC: only users with project-admin or org-admin roles may create or assign profiles.
- Audit logs: every profile create/update/delete emits an audit event stored for 365 days (configurable).
- Data residency: profile metadata contains no customer data; preview mode that ingests sample traffic is processed in the region of the request per Private deployment settings.

Packaging and pricing guidance
------------------------------
New SKUs and packages:
- Optimize Add-on (Dedicated/Private): monthly per-cluster fee + usage tier. Includes: unlimited profiles, 90-day analytics retention, 4 hours/month of SRE advisory for profile tuning.
- Optimize Basic (Hosted): included with hosted plans but limited to 3 profiles and 30-day retention.

Pricing principles:
- Value-based: customers who save >15% on unit costs should see ROI in <3 months.
- Simple: pricing tiers should be easy to compare to existing Dedicated commitments.

Suggested price bands (internal guidance):
- Dedicated Optimize Add-on: $2,500 / month per reserved capacity block + metered usage $0.20 per 1M tokens saved-equivalent (billing tracks estimated cost delta).
- Private: negotiation-based with minimum platform fee $10,000 / month for on-prem engagements.

Billing events and metrics to expose:
- profile-enablement.timestamp
- estimated-monthly-savings (reported on dashboard for customers)
- billing-usage-summary (monthly)

Docs & enablement artifacts to publish
-------------------------------------
- Customer-facing: Quickstart guide (how to create and apply profiles), Best-practices playbook, Pricing FAQ, Pilot checklist.
- Internal: Runbook for SRE support, billing integration spec, sales enablement deck (ROI scenarios).

Open risks and mitigations
-------------------------
- Risk: Customers misconfigure profiles causing quality regressions.
  Mitigation: Preview simulator, conservative default profiles, mandatory canary rollout steps in docs.
- Risk: Billing calculation complexity.
  Mitigation: Early alignment with finance and exposing clear estimated-savings metrics.
- Risk: Runtime performance regressions from frequent profile changes.
  Mitigation: Cache CPS responses in runtime; profile changes trigger soft-update and controlled draining.

Roadmap and themes (Q1 2026 — Q4 2026)
--------------------------------------
Q1 2026 (completed)
- Prototype CPS and console mockups.
- Internal telemetry hooks added to runtime.

Q2 2026 (current focus)
- Deliver CPS v1 with CRUD API, console editor, and runtime integration for batching and KV TTLs.
- Start customer pilots.

Q3 2026
- GA release for Hosted and Dedicated; enable Optimize Add-on SKU.
- Add advanced analytics (per-prompt cost attribution) and extended retention.

Q4 2026
- Expand quantization workflows (tie into quantization-profiles epic) and model conversion tooling for Private customers.
- Introduce automated profile recommendations in console (ML-driven).

Release notes (v1.0.0-beta -> v1.0.0-GA)
---------------------------------------
v1.0.0-beta (internal dogfood, 2026-01-12)
- Features: CPS CRUD API, console create/edit, runtime preview endpoint.
- Known issues: Preview estimation underestimates cost for extremely bursty traffic patterns.

v1.0.0 (pilot release, 2026-03-22)
- Features: Per-route profile assignment, autoscaler signal integration, basic analytics dashboard.
- Pilot feedback: Improved default low-latency profile required; increased default batch_window_ms reduced latency but increased cost for small payloads.

v1.1.0 (beta to all Dedicated, 2026-06-15)
- Features: Billing SKU enabled, CLI simulation tool, extended analytics retention to 90 days for Optimize Add-on trials.
- Breaking changes: None. Default runtime behavior unchanged for routes without profiles.

Support and escalation
----------------------
- Tier 1: Customer Success (Sana Kapoor) — initial triage and simulation help.
- Tier 2: Eng-Serving-Runtime (Priya Nair) — runtime integration issues.
- Escalation playbook: standard oncall page: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks -> follow incident process, attach profile_id and sample traffic payload.

Appendices
---------
A. CLI snippets
1) Create profile from file:
rwi cost-profile create --file cost-profile.yaml --org my-org --project demo
2) Simulate with sample traffic:
rwi cost-profile simulate --profile-id pf_1234 --traffic sample-traffic.json --region us-west-2

B. Example profiles
- low-latency (p50 30ms): small batches, float16, short KV TTLs.
- cost-optimized (p50 80ms): larger batch windows, int8 if available, longer KV TTLs.

C. Related pages
